raw_segments.text: Caliban. Why, as I told thee, tease accustomed with him, I th afternoon to sleep. There thou
mayst brain him, having first seized his books, or with a log batter his skull, or paunch
him with a steak, or cut his wesund with thy knife. Remember first to possess his books,
for without them he is but a sot, as I am, nor hath not one spirit to command. They all
do hate him as rootedly as I burn but his books. He has brave utensils for so he calls
them which when he has a house, he'll deck with all, and that most deeply to consider
is the beauty of his daughter. He himself calls her a nonpareil. I never saw a woman,
but only Sycorax my dam and she. But she as far surpasseth Sycorax as Greatstee does least.
